segments.text: A Semantic Confidence–Aware Intuitionistic Fuzzy Ranking Algorithm for Product Evaluation Using Online Reviews Abstract-Online product reviews have become an important source of consumer purchase decision making, but effectively ranking competing products from the large-scale, opinion-rich review data is a challenging task due to semantic ambiguity, sentiment uncertainty and reviewer subjectivity. State-of-the-art rating methods only base on single value sentiment or intervals obtained by classifier randomness which cannot fully represent the confidence, strength and reliability of expressed reviews. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a novel technique called Semantic Confidence–Aware Intuitionistic Fuzzy Ranking (SICA-IFR). The model capitalizes on both contextual semantic representations and confidence-aware sentiment modeling to enhance robustness and interpretability in product ranking. At first, the context em- beddings are utilized to encode the attribute-specific review texts with fine-grained semantic information retained. Afterwards we use more than one sentiment classifiers, such as positive, neutral and negative orientations. Unlike traditional ensemble methods, SCA-IFR embodies a semantic agreement in its framework that evaluates multi-classifier consensus and the intensity of opinion, thus enabling it to produce confidence-weighted sentiment intervals. These ranges are represented using intuitionistic fuzzy sets where support, opposition and hesitance present in the online reviews are considered. In addition, the algorithm includes a data-aware adjustment of attributes weight, to reconcile user preference with sentiment dominance discovered in review. Final product evaluations are performed by an intuitionistic fuzzy TOPSIS model. Experimental results on real-world product review datasets show that our model SCA-IFR significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art review-based ranking algorithms, with approximately 8.7% improvement in average ranking accuracy, about 12.4% reduction of the rank variance and around 10.1% increase of decision stability in different sentiment distributions. These findings validate that the suggested method gives more reliable and consumer-oriented product rankings, for which it is applicable for intelligent decision-support systems in e-commerce environments. Keywords-Product ranking, Online reviews, Semantic confidence, Intuitionistic fuzzy sets, TOPSIS, Sentiment analysis, Decision support systems I Introduction​ The recent growth of online shopping has changed the way people discover [1][2], assess and purchase goods. Today's purchase decisions are heavily influenced by online reviews, which reflect real experiences [3][4], perceived value and product deficiencies. In contrast to conventional star-rating systems, textual reviews also duplicate rich information, such as feature-specific view-points of users and the emotional tone used in their expression. The task of mining such information out and transforming it into trustworthy product rankings is thus crucial for recommendation systems, consumer decision support, and intelligent marketplace management [5][6]. Nonetheless, it is challenging to build a good product-ranking model due to dynamic reviews, large scale and rich opinions of review data.
segments.label: human

segments.text: While abundant review information can be taken advantage of, there are still a few open issues associated with the current ranking methodologies [7][8]. Natural language reviews are ambiguous First, natural language review can be ambiguous since it conveys meaning based on context, sarcasm or implicit sentiment in different ways. Second, sentiment in reviews is inherently uncertain: users often express positive and negative opinions within the same review, posing polarity assignment as a challenging problem. Third, reviewing is subjective and findings may be relative to the review expectation of readers based on usage scenario and writing style as well [9][10]. Last but not least, the majority of prior systems involve relatively less study on modeling confidence in predicted sentiments for the lack of quantisation of opinion extraction. In the current review-based ranking models [11], sentiment information is often collapsed into only one score which oversimplifies complex feelings and throws away important reliability clues [12]. Some recent work tries to correct for uncertainty by providing interval estimates on the basis of classifier randomisation, although these intervals rarely correspond accurately to semantic alignment between classifiers [13][14]. On the other hand, fuzzy and intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning have been studied about decision making under uncertain information; however, how to use these methods in combination with contextual semantics of labels and classifier confidence is insufficiently paid attention with them. Hence, rankings produced by these methods may vary given different sentiment distributions and might not accurately reflect the customer attitude [15]. To compensate these deficiencies, in this paper we propose a Semantic Confidence–Aware Intuitionistic Fuzzy Ranking (SCA-IFR) algorithm to effectively evaluate products based on online reviews. The proposed model integrates context semantic representations and confidence-aware sentiment modeling to represent the opinions with both their meaning and reliability. Our method begins with encoding attribute-level review texts with contextual embeddings that capture fine-grained semantics [16][17]. We finally use several sentiment classifiers and aggregate their output with a semantic agreement mechanism to measure the level of positivity or negativity from the opinion. The confidence-weighted intervals are formulated as intuitionistic fuzzy sets so that the explicit representation of support, opposition, and indecisiveness can be kept in reviews [18][19]. Finally, a data-driven weighting approach and an intuitionistic fuzzy-TOPSIS method leads stable and explainable rankings of products. We can summarize the main contributions of this work as: ●​ A holistic semantic confidence-aware framework that combines context word embeddings with multi-class sentiment modeling for capturing both opinion meaning and the confidence of opinions. ●​ A semantic-agreement–based intuitionistic fuzzy modeling approach, capturing for support, opposition and hesitance with confidence weighted sentiment intervals. ●​ An intuitionistic fuzzy TOPSIS ranking method which is capable of generating consistent, understandable and consumer- oriented product rankings under different sentiment states. In line with these contributions, the study is guided by the following research objectives:
segments.label: human

segments.text: ●​ To build a review-ranked model with consideration of semantic context, sentiment uncertainty and classifier confidence. ●​ To develop a confidence-conscious intuitionistic fuzzy representation model for hesitation and disagreement on opinions. ●​ To evaluate the proposed framework against advanced models ranking approaches and to verify its improvement in accuracy, robustness, and decision stability. 1.1 Organization of the paper: The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II reviews existing studies on review-based ranking, fuzzy decision models, and confidence-aware sentiment analysis. Section III explains the proposed SCA-IFR framework, including semantic modeling, multi-classifier confidence estimation, and intuitionistic fuzzy ranking. Section IV describes the datasets, experimental setup, and evaluation metrics, while Section V presents and discusses the results. Finally, Section VI concludes the work and outlines future research directions. Together with these advances, the overall achievements illustrate steady progress of fusing fuzzy logic, psychological modeling and data-driven sentiment processing in building more realistic decision-support systems. 2.5 Gaps Identified Despite the great achievements in previous work, two significant limitations are shared. ●​ While predicting sentiment, most models predict the sentiment of a sentence as a discrete value and do not consider the uncertainty caused by classifier disagreement, linguistic vagueness, and contextual variation. ●​ There are few such models jointly considering semantic under- standing and confidence, particularly in the case of intuitionistic fuzzy structures to handle not only strength of agreement, but also strength of doubt. These deficiencies provide the motivation for devising the SCA-IFR framework, which explicitly considers contextual semantics, classifier consensus and confidence-weighted intuitionistic fuzzy modeling to produce more stable and credible rankings of products. III Methodology​ Our proposed SCA-IFR framework converts raw online reviews into a reliable product ranking based on unified pipeline that fuses semantic modeling, classifier confidence and intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning. First, the reviews are preprocessed, and then correlated with product attributes. And the remaining part of each attribute-specific textual segment is encoded by contextualized embeddings to retain fine-grained semantics [17][18]. These encoded representations of the text are then evaluated by multi-class sentiment classifiers, each of which creates a separate probability distribution for positive, neutral, and negative attitudes. We employ a semantic agreement measure to estimate the inter-classifier agreement and how well classifiers align with contextual semantics, computing confidence-weighted sentiment intervals. These spans are then transformed into intuitionistic fuzzy values, which explicitly reflect on the support, opposition and hesitation [19][20]. Finally, based on user preferences and sentiment dominance, the weight of the attribute is obtained via an intuitionistic fuzzy TOPSIS algorithm to calculate closeness coefficients that rank the products. This combination results in a robust, interpretable and real consumer judgment consistent SCA-IFR ranking computation.

segments.text: Fig 3 shows an end to tread approach of the model from review collection and pre-processing, semantic embedding to multi-classifier sentiment estimation. Semantic agreement and confidence weighting are then utilized, then intuitionistic fuzzy modeling and IF-TOPSIS ranking are used to produce the final ranked list. The proposed workflow demonstrates how to combine semantics and confidence in the aggregation of decisions to attain better reliability. IV Implementation details 4.1 Datasets We validate our approach using the Cleaned Amazon Sales and Reviews Dataset taken from Kaggle, which is made up of a set of curated product records along with the corresponding review data extracted from the Amazon electronics marketplace (CSV format, UTF-8 encoded). This dataset has 4,854 product–review tuples, each representing a review of some product out of its 4,467 products with the following attributes: name and brand (product detail), price and discount percentage (product trading status), numerical rating and text review from users of the product (user sentiment toward that product) as well as cleaned review text and sentiment label. Since the dataset has already gone through pre-processing (non-preference, missing value treatment and fields standardised) it can be directly used for sentiment modelling and ranking analysis. In the case of machine-learning experiments, the data are split 80:20 resulting in a training set with 3,883 instances and a test set containing 971 instances; thus we can evaluate classifier performance and stability downstream. 4.2 Experimental Setup​ The purpose of these experiments was to test the efficacy of the proposed SCA-IFR framework for ordering products based on online reviews. We experimented with the Kaggle cleaned dataset of Amazon sales and reviews that consists of 4,854 review records for 4,467 products with 11 attributes. Pre-processed YourDailyMenu review text were loaded, that include lemon juice.and then tokenized and lower-cased with punctuation, URL stop-word removed. We extracted contextual semantic representations using a pretrained BERT base model (hidden size = 768) that was fine-tuned on the training corpus learning rate, 2 × 10 −5 batch size 16, max sequence length = 128. As a comparison, we also trained an SVM with RBF kernel and a Bi-LSTM network (hidden size = 128, dropout = 0.3). For neural models we used cross-entropy loss, and Adam optimizer and early stopping based on validation loss. The numbers of training and test samples were 3,883 and 971 respectively in the ratio of 80:20. The output of all classifiers was calibrated to probability distributions and these were then used to calculate the semantic agreement and confidence-weighted intervals. The intuitionistic fuzzy decision matrices thus obtained were standardized and ranked by the proposed IFTOPSIS approach. For comparison with robustness, we also confronted SCA-IFR using (i) sentiment ranking by a single classifier, (ii) classical fuzzy TOPSIS, and (iii) since we have only confidence values on the intuitionistic fuzzy set without any representation of the degree of hesitance or extremism over reference values for alternatives in IFset. We tested based on ranking accuracy, Kendall’s rank correlation, variance of ranking position across runs and decision stability in case of perturbed sentiment

It has been compared with some of well known ranking approaches using existing review based benchmarks in order to prove its definite advantages in realistic decision-support applications. We evaluate performance metrics with the publicly available Amazon review dataset and perform numerous experiments for consistency and fairness. In brief, to combine the semantic certainty with IFR a great enhancement is the reliable and consumer-oriented product ranking. 5.1 Overall Ranking Performance several existing review-based ranking approaches. Three criteria, being ranking accuracy, ranking variance and decision stability are considered in the analysis. Together, these measures can help indicate whether a model is able to reproduce the actual order of competing products that customers liked better or worse on average run-to-run and across different types of noisy or imbalanced sentiment input. As presented in Table 1 and Figure 1–3, SCA-IFR consistently achieves better performance than the baselines. The benefits

We compare it with a variant of the complete SCA-IFR model that uses intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning to isolate its effect but ignores confidence weighting. A comparison of the results in Table 2 indicates that with incorporating semantic agreement and confidence intervals significant improvements are achieved with respect to accuracy, ranking variance and decision stability. These observations leave no doubt that, it is indeed crucial to model the consensuality and opinionated nature of classifiers disagreement as we consider it here, in order to avoid uncertain or weakly supported sentiments from biasing ultimately the ranking of the final product. Ablation study verifies that the performance improvements accumulate with semantic representation, multiclassifier fusion and intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning, where confidence-aware modeling contributes most to the superiority. These results suggest that ranks obtained by SCA-IFR are more robust in the face of classifier disagreement and review

In general, the discussion reveals that one needs to model both opinion content and confidence in order to have realistic decision-support for e-commerce applications. VI Conclusion This work presented a Semantic Confidence-Aware Intuitionistic Fuzzy Ranking (SCA-IFR) model for product rating based on online reviews. Combining the bag of words with topical semantic embeddings, multi-classifier sentiment estimation process and a Semantic Agreement Measure and intuitionistic fuzzy TOPSIS model, can more effectively measure the meaning of as well as the reliability in expressed opinions. Empirical results on real review data indicate that the SCA-IFR is superior to other existing ranking methods, with improvements of 8.7% in average ranking accuracy, 12.45% in average reduction of ranking variance and 10.1% in decision stability over others are observed. Results show that confidence-aware modeling approach yields more robust and interpretable ranks, which are closer to consumer' judgment. As future work, we will investigate how to integrate the reviewer credibility and fake-review detection into the ranking approach. Furthermore, Generalizing SCA-IFR in order to deal with multi-site, multilingual review environment would be an interesting research direction. References [1] Salminen, J., Kandpal, C., Kamel, A.
